label: CACNA1A
summary_plain: Builds pore-forming alpha-1A subunit of P/Q-type calcium channel essential for neurotransmitter release.

label: ATP1A2
summary_plain: Encodes sodium/potassium ATPase alpha-2 subunit that regulates glial ion balance and glutamate clearance.

label: SCN1A
summary_plain: Encodes voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.1 critical for GABAergic inhibitory interneuron firing.

label: KCNA1
summary_plain: Encodes voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.1 controlling repolarization in cerebellar basket cells.

label: CACNB4
summary_plain: Encodes calcium channel beta-4 auxiliary subunit that modulates Cav2.1 and Cav2.2 trafficking.

label: SLC1A3
summary_plain: Encodes excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (GLAST) clearing synaptic glutamate in Bergmann glia.

label: ATXN1
summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-1; CAG repeat expansion causes cerebellar Purkinje cell neurodegeneration.

label: ATXN2
summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-2; polyglutamine expansion impairs RNA metabolism and translation.

label: ATXN3
summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-3 deubiquitinase; polyQ expansion leads to toxic protein aggregates.

label: ATXN7
summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-7 subunit of STAGA complex; polyQ expansion causes ataxia with macular degeneration.

label: CACNA1B
summary_plain: Encodes N-type voltage-gated calcium channel pore subunit closely related to Cav2.1.

label: CACNA1E
summary_plain: Encodes R-type calcium channel alpha-1E subunit implicated in early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.

label: Episodic Ataxia Type 2
summary_plain: Recurrent attacks of unsteadiness, vertigo, and slurred speech lasting hours, triggered by stress or exertion.

label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 1
summary_plain: Severe migraines accompanied by temporary weakness on one side of the body and visual disturbances.

label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 6
summary_plain: Gradual, progressive loss of balance and coordination beginning in mid-to-late adulthood.

label: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy 42
summary_plain: Severe early-onset seizures, developmental arrest or regression, and muscle tone abnormalities.

label: Episodic Ataxia Type 1
summary_plain: Brief attacks of ataxia and persistent muscle rippling (myokymia) caused by potassium channel defects.

label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 2
summary_plain: Migraines with motor weakness caused by pump defects that disrupt brain potassium and glutamate removal.

label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 3
summary_plain: Migraines with transient motor weakness caused by gain-of-function sodium channel Nav1.1 variants.

label: Episodic Ataxia Type 5
summary_plain: Paroxysmal ataxia episodes caused by mutations in the calcium channel beta-4 auxiliary subunit.

label: Episodic Ataxia Type 6
summary_plain: Episodic ataxia with seizures and hemiplegia caused by impaired glial glutamate uptake transporter.

label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 1
summary_plain: Progressive neurodegenerative cerebellar ataxia caused by CAG polyglutamine expansion in ATXN1.

label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2
summary_plain: Autosomal dominant progressive ataxia with slow saccadic eye movements caused by ATXN2 CAG expansion.

label: Machado-Joseph Disease (SCA3)
summary_plain: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with spasticity and peripheral neuropathy caused by ATXN3 CAG expansion.

label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 7
summary_plain: Adult-onset progressive cerebellar ataxia accompanied by progressive cone-rod retinal dystrophy.

label: Dravet Syndrome
summary_plain: Severe childhood epilepsy syndrome commonly triggered by fever and linked to SCN1A channel loss of function.

label: Cav2.1 Loss of Function
summary_plain: Decreased calcium influx at presynaptic terminals impairs neurotransmitter release in cerebellar circuits.

label: Cav2.1 Gain of Function
summary_plain: Increased calcium influx at lower voltages facilitates cortical spreading depression and migraine aura.

label: Polyglutamine CAG Expansion Toxicity
summary_plain: Abnormally long glutamine tracts cause protein misfolding, aggregate buildup, and Purkinje cell death.

label: Cortical Spreading Depression
summary_plain: A slow wave of cellular depolarization in the cerebral cortex that triggers migraine aura and headache.

label: Purkinje Cell Pacemaking Instability
summary_plain: Loss of regular high-frequency firing in Purkinje cells disrupts motor coordination outputs.

label: Glutamate Clearance Impairment
summary_plain: Failure of astrocytic pumps or transporters leads to excessive extracellular glutamate and hyperexcitability.

label: CACNA1A c.575G>A (p.Arg192Gln)
summary_plain: Well-characterized gain-of-function missense variant causing familial hemiplegic migraine type 1.

label: CACNA1A c.653C>T (p.Ser218Leu)
summary_plain: Severe gain-of-function mutation causing hemiplegic migraine, delayed cerebral edema, and coma after mild trauma.

label: CACNA1A c.1994C>T (p.Thr665Met) (legacy T666M)
summary_plain: Pore region gain-of-function mutation causing severe familial hemiplegic migraine type 1.

label: CACNA1A c.4633C>T (p.Arg1545Ter)
summary_plain: Nonsense truncating mutation causing loss of Cav2.1 channel function and episodic ataxia type 2.

label: CACNA1A c.4979G>A (p.Arg1660His) (legacy R1666H)
summary_plain: Recurrent de novo missense variant causing severe developmental delay and early epileptic encephalopathy.

label: Ataxia
summary_plain: Lack of voluntary coordination of muscle movements including gait and limb control.

label: Episodic ataxia
summary_plain: Sudden recurring episodes of unsteady balance and clumsiness.

label: Nystagmus
summary_plain: Rhythmic, involuntary movements of the eyes, often triggered by looking sideways.

label: Dysarthria
summary_plain: Difficulty speaking clearly due to impaired coordination of speech muscles.

label: Migraine with aura
summary_plain: Severe headaches preceded by sensory or visual changes such as flashing lights.

label: Hemiplegia
summary_plain: Temporary or permanent paralysis affecting one side of the body.

label: Seizure
summary_plain: Sudden, uncontrolled electrical disturbance in the brain altering behavior or awareness.

label: Cerebral edema
summary_plain: Accumulation of fluid in brain tissues that can cause pressure and coma after head trauma.

label: Global developmental delay
summary_plain: Delayed attainment of motor, language, cognitive, or social milestones in childhood.

label: Vertigo
summary_plain: Sensation that the room is spinning or moving when standing or sitting.

label: Hypotonia
summary_plain: Decreased muscle tone causing floppiness and delayed motor development.

label: Dystonia
summary_plain: Twisting, repetitive movements or abnormal postures caused by involuntary muscle contractions.

label: Spasticity
summary_plain: Condition in which muscles stiffen or tighten, preventing normal fluid movement.

label: Cerebellar atrophy
summary_plain: Progressive loss of tissue in the cerebellum visible on brain MRI scans.

label: Delayed speech and language development
summary_plain: Late development of speech and expressive language skills in early childhood.

label: Progressive cerebellar ataxia
summary_plain: Slowly worsening lack of coordination and balance over years.

label: Headache
summary_plain: Pain in the head or upper neck commonly accompanying migraine or paroxysmal neurological attacks.

label: Acetazolamide
summary_plain: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor reducing episodic ataxia attacks by modifying pH and extracellular ions.

label: 4-Aminopyridine
summary_plain: Potassium channel blocker that restores regular pacemaking in Purkinje cells to prevent ataxia attacks.

label: Verapamil
summary_plain: L-type calcium channel blocker used off-label for prophylaxis against hemiplegic migraine attacks.

label: Flunarizine
summary_plain: Dual calcium and sodium antagonist used internationally for migraine prophylaxis.

label: Troriluzole
summary_plain: Prodrug of riluzole designed to enhance glial glutamate uptake and reduce cerebellar excitotoxicity.

label: Sodium Valproate
summary_plain: Broad-spectrum anticonvulsant and migraine preventive agent enhancing GABA neurotransmission.

label: Lamotrigine
summary_plain: Voltage-gated sodium channel blocker used for seizure prevention and migraine aura prophylaxis.

label: Levetiracetam
summary_plain: Antiepileptic drug binding SV2A vesicle protein to moderate neurotransmitter release in refractory seizures.

label: Topiramate
summary_plain: Broad-acting channel modulator and mild carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used for migraine prevention.

label: CACNA1A Foundation
summary_plain: Leading international patient advocacy organization supporting families and funding CACNA1A research.

label: National Ataxia Foundation
summary_plain: US advocacy group dedicated to accelerating treatments and cure for all forms of ataxia including EA2 and SCA6.

label: Ataxia UK
summary_plain: UK charity providing support, clinical guidelines, and research funding for cerebellar ataxias.

label: Euro-Ataxia
summary_plain: Federation of national ataxia patient associations in Europe coordinating transnational advocacy.

label: Ataxia Global Initiative
summary_plain: Worldwide platform uniting clinicians, patient advocates, and industry for trial readiness in ataxias.

label: Rare Epilepsy Network
summary_plain: Collaborative network connecting rare developmental and epileptic encephalopathy communities.

label: Dravet Syndrome Foundation
summary_plain: Patient organization funding channelopathy research and family support for SCN1A-related seizures.

label: The Migraine Trust
summary_plain: UK charity funding research, promoting awareness, and providing support for severe migraine conditions.

label: CACNA1A Connect (patient registry)
summary_plain: Registry where families share medical history so research reflects real life.

label: CACNA1A Natural History Study (Chung Lab, Boston Children's Hospital)
summary_plain: Long-term study following people with CACNA1A conditions to learn how symptoms change over time.

label: Tottering Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg)
summary_plain: Recessive mouse model with Cacna1a mutation exhibiting episodic dystonia, absence seizures, and mild ataxia.

label: Leaner Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg-la)
summary_plain: Severe loss-of-function Cacna1a splicing mutant mouse showing cerebellar granule and Purkinje neurodegeneration.

label: Rolling Nagoya Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg-rol)
summary_plain: Spontaneous mouse mutant with reduced Cav2.1 channel activity displaying severe motor ataxia.

label: R192Q Knock-in Mouse Model
summary_plain: Gain-of-function knock-in mouse displaying lowered threshold and accelerated propagation of cortical spreading depression.

label: S218L Knock-in Mouse Model
summary_plain: Severe gain-of-function model displaying susceptibility to lethal seizures and brain edema after mild concussive trigger.

label: 4-Aminopyridine in Episodic Ataxia Type 2
summary_plain: Planned placebo-controlled trial of 4-aminopyridine in episodic ataxia type 2. It was withdrawn before enrolling.

label: Troriluzole in Adult Participants With Spinocerebellar Ataxia
summary_plain: Phase 3 clinical trial testing troriluzole efficacy in patients with spinocerebellar ataxias including SCA6.

label: Natural History Study of and Genetic Modifiers in Spinocerebellar Ataxias
summary_plain: Longitudinal natural history study by the Clinical Research Consortium for SCAs.

label: Arn M.J.M. van den Maagdenberg
summary_plain: Professor at Leiden University Medical Center; pioneering investigator bridging FHM1, EA2, and Cav2.1 channel biology.

label: Joanna C. Jen
summary_plain: Professor of Neurology at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; international authority on Episodic Ataxia 2 and neurogenetics.

label: Michael Strupp
summary_plain: Professor of Neurology at LMU Munich; pioneered 4-aminopyridine as medical therapy for episodic ataxia and cerebellar dysfunction.

label: Christopher M. Gomez
summary_plain: Professor at University of Chicago; discovered CACNA1A bicistronic expression of alpha1ACT driving SCA6 pathology.

label: Wendy K. Chung
summary_plain: Chief of Pediatrics at Boston Children's / Harvard; principal investigator of the CACNA1A natural history study.

label: Daniela Pietrobon
summary_plain: Professor of Physiology at University of Padua; leading expert on biophysical gating mechanisms of Cav2.1 mutants in migraine.

label: Robert W. Baloh
summary_plain: Emeritus Professor of Neurology at UCLA; clinical pioneer who characterized episodic ataxia types and vestibulocerebellar disorders.

label: Thomas Klockgether
summary_plain: Director at DZNE Bonn; international leader of the EUROSCA natural history consortium in degenerative ataxias.

label: Stefan M. Pulst
summary_plain: Chair of Neurology at University of Utah; leader in spinocerebellar ataxia genetics, Purkinje cell channelopathy, and antisense therapies.

label: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
summary_plain: US federal institute funding biomedical research on the nervous system, channelopathies, and rare neurogenetic diseases.

label: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Rare As One
summary_plain: Philanthropic foundation providing grant funding and organizational capacity to rare disease patient communities.

label: European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases (EJP RD)
summary_plain: European research consortium funding transnational collaborative research and registries for rare diseases.

label: Ophoff et al. 1996 (Cell)
summary_plain: Landmark paper discovering that CACNA1A mutations cause both familial hemiplegic migraine and episodic ataxia type-2.

label: Zhuchenko et al. 1997 (Nat Genet)
summary_plain: Discovered that small CAG repeat expansions in CACNA1A cause spinocerebellar ataxia type 6.

label: van den Maagdenberg et al. 2004 (Neuron)
summary_plain: Engineered human Cacna1a R192Q knock-in migraine mouse model displaying increased cortical spreading depression.

label: Strupp et al. 2004 (Neurology)
summary_plain: Demonstrated successful clinical treatment of episodic ataxia type 2 attacks with potassium channel blocker 4-aminopyridine.

label: Du et al. 2013 (Cell)
summary_plain: Discovered that a second cistron within CACNA1A encodes alpha1ACT transcription factor driving SCA6 neurodegeneration.

label: Indelicato & Boesch 2026 (Cerebellum)
summary_plain: Demonstrated genotype and age-at-onset drive vermian cerebellar atrophy in CACNA1A-related ataxias.

label: Kessi et al. 2023 (Front Mol Neurosci)
summary_plain: Genotype-phenotype review of CACNA1A-related childhood neurodevelopmental disorders and epileptic encephalopathy.

label: Tottene et al. 2009 (Neuron)
summary_plain: Demonstrated that enhanced synaptic glutamate release underlies spreading depression susceptibility in Cav2.1 knock-in mice.

label: De Fusco et al. 2003 (Nat Genet)
summary_plain: Identified haploinsufficiency of ATP1A2 encoding Na+/K+ pump alpha-2 subunit in familial hemiplegic migraine type 2.

label: Dichgans et al. 2005 (Lancet)
summary_plain: Identified mutation in neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel SCN1A in familial hemiplegic migraine.

label: Browne et al. 1994 (Nat Genet)
summary_plain: Proved episodic ataxia/myokymia syndrome is caused by mutations in voltage-gated potassium channel KCNA1.

label: Jen et al. 2005 (Neurology)
summary_plain: Discovered that mutation in glutamate transporter EAAT1 (SLC1A3) causes episodic ataxia, hemiplegia, and seizures.

label: Jacobi et al. 2015 (Lancet Neurol)
summary_plain: Long-term prospective disease progression study of spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, and 6 in EUROSCA cohort.

label: Pivotal Study of N-acetyl-L-leucine for CACNA1A
summary_plain: Phase 3 trial now recruiting people with CACNA1A conditions (SCA6, EA2, FHM1) to test N-acetyl-L-leucine against placebo.
